clue.text: Scrap with new head, French politician

indicators.note: a new head means the first letter of the word for scrap is swapped for a different one

parts.note: to scrap something is to discard it

explanation.surface: A row breaks out, and a politician across the Channel gets a fresh leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new head' swaps the D at the front of DISCARD for G; the clue does not say which letter, so the definition has to pin it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Valéry Giscard d'Estaing was President of France from 1974 to 1981.

clue.text: First attempt at numbers

parts.note: a go is an attempt or try
L and D are the Roman numerals for fifty and five hundred

explanation.surface: Someone makes an opening try at arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' reads like part of the phrase 'first attempt', but it is the definition: first place wins the top medal. 'at' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever comes first in a race wins the top medal, so gold stands for first place.

clue.text: Pacific element, for example, in which beheaded archbishop is on horse

indicators.note: the word for 'for example' takes the following pieces inside it

parts.note: 'say' introduces an example, as in 'a fruit, say, an apple'

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes before it
beheading removes the first letter of the archbishop's name

parts.note: Lanfranc was the Archbishop of Canterbury under William the Conqueror
taken as written
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: An odd scene: a headless churchman perched on a horse, somehow standing for a Pacific feature.
explanation.walkthrough: Lanfranc was the Norman Archbishop of Canterbury, and 'say' is a way of introducing an example; most solvers first take the horse to be the closing BAY.
explanation.definitionFit: This large bay in California opens onto the Pacific Ocean, so it is one part of that ocean.

clue.text: A sweet girl's name for a flier

parts.note: Irma la Douce, 'Irma the Sweet', is the heroine of the French musical and film

explanation.surface: Someone picks a pretty girl's name to christen a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet girl' depends on knowing Irma la Douce, where douce is French for sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: An airman is someone who flies aircraft, especially a pilot in an air force.

clue.text: Clue for time at south of France causes row

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Clue for time at south of France causes row' (DUSTUP) is a reverse clue: the answer read as instruction, UP (turn upwards in a down light) applied to T (time) + SUD (French south). The only parse is a reverse reading over the whole phrase, which the check refuses (reverse_phrase).
annotationWithheld.clue: Clue for time at south of France causes row

clue.text: Back strike's target, what's caused by atmospheric pollution

indicators.note: back tells us to read the whole phrase 'strike's target' from right to left

parts.note: to lam is to strike or thrash, and the 's adds an S
an aim is a target to hit

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a counterattack should hit, and what smog brings about.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMS + AIM read backwards gives the answer; 'what's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a poisonous or foul vapour in the air, so miasmal describes something that comes from tainted air.

clue.text: Roman patron's mother changed a scene

parts.note: ma is an everyday word for mother

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of 'a scene' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mother redecorates the stage set for her Roman benefactor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after patron is a link ('is'), not part of the definition, and 'changed' acts only on the three letters plus scene that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Maecenas was a wealthy friend of Augustus who backed Virgil and Horace, and his name became a byword for an arts sponsor.

clue.text: Much of the new world bogus, according to Bucks town

indicators.note: much of a word means most of it, so its ending is dropped

parts.note: the Americas were called the New World by European settlers
something bogus is a sham

explanation.surface: A Buckinghamshire town declares most of the Americas fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much of' cuts ICA from AMERICA to leave AMER. Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county north-west of London; 'according to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Amersham is a market town in Buckinghamshire, at the end of a London Underground line.

clue.text: Salad from Damascus with doctor's rent settled

indicators.note: settled suggests the jumbled letters are sorted into a new order

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A Syrian landlord's bill comes with a side salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled' rearranges DAMASCUS + DRS + RENT; here the 's of doctor's does give a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This pairing of seedling greens is a traditional British salad and sandwich filling, often grown on a windowsill.

clue.text: Wild celandine by river, one without a partner

indicators.note: wild suggests the flower's letters are running free in a new order

explanation.surface: A wild flower grows by the water, all on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges CELANDINE into LINEDANCE; 'by' joins R to it.
explanation.definitionFit: In this kind of dance people stand in rows and do the steps alone, without a partner.

clue.text: Moony held by Fiennes retreating

indicators.note: retreating means the letters found are read backwards
held by says the answer is kept within the explorer's first name, with its tail left out

parts.note: Sir Ranulph Fiennes is the British polar explorer

explanation.surface: A dreamy person is kept back by the explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiennes stands for Ranulph Fiennes; 'held by' keeps RANUL from RANULPH, dropping PH, and 'retreating' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Moony can mean of the moon, the same sense as lunar.

clue.text: Among returned negatives there's a 50% chance of finding the author of …

indicators.note: among says one piece is put in the middle of the other
returned means the negatives are read from right to left

parts.note: nots are negatives, like 'no'
evens are betting odds of one to one, a fifty-fifty chance

explanation.surface: Among a pile of rejections, there's an even chance of tracking down a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the definition into the next clue, so the author meant is the writer of Treasure Island; evens are fifty-fifty betting odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote the pirate adventure novel that the next clue describes.

clue.text: … 1 down (and too much Silver) on 12 or in 2

definitions.text: … 1 down (and too much Silver) on 12 or in 2

parts.words: 1 down (and too much Silver) on 12 or in 2
parts.note: the gold of 1 down and Long John Silver go aboard the ship of 12 down in the novel, and there is a real island of this name in the bay at 2 down

explanation.walkthrough: It finishes the previous clue: the novel by STEVENSON. GOLD is the treasure, Long John Silver the pirate, HISPANIOLA the ship, and an artificial island of the same name sits in SAN FRANCISCO BAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's hunt for buried gold, with Long John Silver and the ship Hispaniola, is this book; the bay at 2 holds a real island so named.

clue.text: A ship with a lion adrift went to 11

indicators.note: adrift suggests the letters have come loose and floated into a new order

explanation.surface: A vessel carrying a lion drifts off course on its voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adrift' rearranges A SHIP + A LION; 'with' joins them. The definition is the ship that sailed to the island in the novel at 11.
explanation.definitionFit: In Stevenson's novel the schooner Hispaniola carries the treasure hunters to the island.

clue.text: Bars for the bar?

parts.note: places that serve drinks, read as the London societies that train and call barristers, 'the bar' being the legal profession

explanation.walkthrough: London's four Inns of Court are the professional bodies every barrister must join.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs are bars, and the Inns of Court are the societies of the legal bar, so one word covers both readings.

clue.text: Flint village with fruit of the forest?

parts.note: a haw is the red berry of the hawthorn
the Forest of Arden is the woodland in Shakespeare's As You Like It

explanation.surface: A Welsh village known for berries from the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: Flint is short for Flintshire, a county in north-east Wales, not the stone; 'with' and 'of the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawarden is a village in Flintshire, once home to the Victorian Prime Minister Gladstone.

clue.text: One boy embracing another is giving the false impression that it's always happening

definitions.text: giving the false impression that it's always happening

indicators.note: embracing means the first boy's name wraps round what follows

parts.note: Tom is a boy's name
Ken is another boy's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: One lad hugging another, which some read as putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests two boys hugging; the definition describes a show of effort that is only skin-deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokenism is making a small symbolic gesture so that an effort looks thorough and constant when it isn't.

clue.text: Wild harebell in Munich, perhaps

definitions.note: the definition describes a place found in Munich, as an example

indicators.note: wild suggests the flower's letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild flower blooms in a Bavarian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges HAREBELL. The definition points to Munich's famous drinking halls, one of which gave its name to Hitler's 1923 putsch.
explanation.definitionFit: Large halls serving beer are a famous feature of Munich, so Munich gives an example of where one is found.

clue.text: I'm inside right: little prince is one first

indicators.note: first says the earlier pieces come before the word for right

parts.note: Pr is a short form of prince
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer playing inside right, with a junior royal ahead of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm inside' looks like a football position, inside right, but it is the definition: someone locked up, speaking in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in jail could say they're inside, the slang for being locked up.

clue.text: Stake and it is quite slow

definitions.meaning: the amount each player puts in before cards are dealt
put after 'and', the word makes the musical direction for a moderately slow pace

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads 'and' + it as a single word: the musical tempo marking ANDANTE, which means fairly slow.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the stake each player puts in up front, and 'and' plus it gives andante, a moderately slow tempo.

clue.text: Missing with cast at channel of speech

indicators.note: missing says the abbreviation for with is left out of the word for cast

parts.note: to cast is to throw
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler misses a fish while casting at a channel.
explanation.walkthrough: W is the standard abbreviation for 'with', so 'Missing with' quietly asks for that one letter to go; the result is the old poetic spelling thro'.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech is made by air passing up the throat, the passage through the neck.

clue.text: Leader of the drunkards, one that's given to street crime

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: sots are habitual drunkards
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The ringleader of a bunch of drinkers is a petty criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: A tsotsi is a South African township thug; the definition reads as 'one who is given to street crime', with the 'one' given by I.
explanation.definitionFit: In South African usage a tsotsi is a young urban gangster or mugger.

clue.text: Modern science needs stated modern and evident remedies

indicators.note: stated says the next word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: something modern is new
something evident is clear
physics is an old word for medicines or remedies

explanation.surface: Modern science calls for up-to-date cures that work in plain sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stated' makes NEW into the sound NU. Physic is an old word for medicine, so 'physics' are remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of atoms and their nuclei is a twentieth-century branch of science.

clue.text: Entrance money, 1 down for 2?

definitions.meaning: the total paid at the turnstiles by spectators at a match
add the gold of 1 down to make the famous bridge spanning the strait into the bay at 2

explanation.walkthrough: GOLD + -EN + this word is the Golden Gate, the strait whose bridge leads into San Francisco Bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is an entrance and also the takings from paying spectators; the Golden Gate is the mouth of San Francisco Bay.

clue.text: Piece of music unsuitable as voluntary?

definitions.text: Piece of music unsuitable as voluntary?

parts.words: Piece of music unsuitable as voluntary?
parts.note: a voluntary is an organ piece, but the answer is a musical part that is compulsory, so it is no free choice

explanation.walkthrough: The term means 'obligatory' in Italian: an accompanying part that must be played. A voluntary is an organ piece, but 'voluntary' also means optional.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an essential instrumental part that cannot be left out, the opposite of optional.

clue.text: The volunteers have a Greek character

parts.note: taken as written
the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: The reservists include someone from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Very bad infant under 7 lbs gets topped and tailed

indicators.note: topped and tailed means losing the first and last letters

parts.note: a baby is an infant
a newborn under seven pounds counts as small

explanation.surface: A tiny newborn being washed top and bottom, a nursery chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' cuts the outer letters off BABY SMALL; topping and tailing is also the British name for washing a baby's face and bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means dreadful, as bad as can be.

clue.text: English in unhappy French city in Italy

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the French word

parts.note: triste is French for sad or unhappy

explanation.surface: An Englishman is miserable in a French city that turns out to be Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city' looks like the definition, but 'French' belongs with 'unhappy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a port city in north-east Italy on the Adriatic.
